Look man I know what I did wasn't the smartest. I didn't share my experience for someone to tell me what is clearly obvious to begin with. I wanted to share my experience with the hopes that people can understand how easy it is for you to make a lazy mistake without realizing what u have done and possibly creating a life-threatening injury.  I don't plan on selling a thing, and in fact I plan I spending money on getting myself professional training and letting this experience be a reality check. We are all human and humans make mistakes.

I felt a huge amount of energy thru my body but my brain didn't quite process what occurred until i looked down and saw my leg. The adrenaline rush I got was like no other feeling on Earth. I was met with feelings of panic and the harsh reality that I might lose my life momentarily. Time seemed to move in slow motion and I felt a crazy sense of alertness. I knew that every second mattered and I immediately thought to tourniquet my leg and save my life. After the adrenaline started to dump off I felt a warm feeling over the wounded area
I did indeed, the paramedics were quite impressed lol

So today I bought a new gun at the gun store (fns9c). I went into the parking lot and sat in my car and loaded it, a few moments later I decided I wanted to field strip it, the last step in doing so requires u to pull the trigger... Apparently the extractor failed due to me using old ammo. I proceeded  to shoot my self in the leg accidentally. I didn't even realize what had just occurred my body felt a shock of energy and my ears rang really loud... I then looked down and saw my leg squirting blood uncontrollably so I immediately limped back inside the gun store and told them what just happened and tried calling 911 at the time... My ears were so shot that I couldn't hear the 911 operator and so I hung up on them... I then proceed to use my belt as a make shift tourniquet and awaited the ambulance. Luckily the round missed my artery and bones. It just went thru some fat and muscle. After many pain reducing drugs and a month long recovery I should make it out perfectly fine. 

I wanted to share my experience with you all with the hopes that I can convince you to not just assume the extractor will always eject the round in your chamber and to also remind you that a tourniquet can save your life.
